source.title: When Life gives you LLMs, make LLM-ADE: Large Language Models with Adaptive Data Engineering

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no truncation or garbling prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates TinyLlama during continued pretraining at successive training intervals, which bears on epoch-wise double descent, but uses a different model setting and benchmark-performance measures rather than a dedicated double-descent experiment.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports benchmark performance through training on SlimPajama and the text describes an immediate drop with no recovery. This bears on V2. The paper also reports effects of duplicative-data mixtures, but does not vary sample count near an interpolation threshold; those results are recorded under fits_no_version. LLM-ADE's own comparison results are not recorded as evidence for double descent because they evaluate the proposed method rather than the claimed curve.
record.test_reason: The paper names double descent only as a risk of continued pretraining that LLM-ADE is said to mitigate. It never measures test error against model size, epochs or sample count. The only training-time curve (Figure 3) shows benchmark accuracy of an already-pretrained TinyLlama during continued pretraining on SlimPajama. The authors label this catastrophic forgetting, which is a different construct from an epoch-wise double-descent trajectory. The remaining results compare the proposed method against CPT and LoRA.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LLM-ADE (block freezing and expansion) beats plain CPT and LoRA, with up to +0.78 average and +0.50 even with 20% SlimPajama. They say it mitigates catastrophic forgetting and double descent, but they assert the double-descent part without measuring it.
record.recipe_differences: Continued pretraining of TinyLlama with benchmark evaluations at successive CPT intervals; the paper does not present a dedicated size, epoch, or sample-count double-descent sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Training data changes the reported outcome: SlimPajama-only CPT causes benchmark performance to drop without recovery, while the paper describes loss of OpenHermes-CPT gains with 10% SlimPajama and performance below the base model with 20%.

fits_no_version.finding: Continued pretraining of TinyLlama solely on SlimPajama, which overlaps its pretraining data, dropped HellaSwag and Winogrande accuracy immediately, with no recovery. The Table 1 average change was -12.00 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued pretraining on data duplicating the pretraining corpus causes catastrophic forgetting of general benchmarks in small LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixing 10% or 20% SlimPajama into OpenHermes CPT reduced the +0.57 average gain to +0.04 and -0.02 respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small fractions of duplicative data erase continued-pretraining gains.

record.problems: The epoch-wise result is shown only in a figure, without numerical values in the text; it covers one model and one training-data setting. The reported measures are benchmark performance rather than explicitly named test error, and no controls or uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the row cap. LLM-ADE mixture results in Table 3 are not included because they evaluate the proposed method's performance, not the claimed double-descent curve.

untested.parts: No test-error-over-epochs curve for a model trained toward interpolation. The Figure 3 forgetting curve does not measure this.
No sample-count sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No label-noise, multiple-peak or regularization tests.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges V2' label is dropped. Figure 3 is a forgetting curve on a pretrained model under distribution shift, not an epoch-wise double-descent test. Table 1 also lists a CPT 100% SlimPajama row at -12.00 average (HellaSwag 31.1, Winogrande 50.0). Preprint with a single model and no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold measurement.
Only TinyLlama trained on SlimPajama is shown; the reported measures are benchmark performance, not explicit test-error values, and other models, datasets, and training settings are not tested.
No sample-count sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No common effective-complexity measure is evaluated.
No test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of model complexity by effective parameters.

rows.subject: TinyLlama
rows.operation_detail: Continued pretraining solely on SlimPajama; benchmark performance plotted at each 1/20th interval of CPT.
rows.value: figure only; text says performance dropped significantly immediately after SlimPajama training began and did not recover during training
rows.note: The text describes a drop without recovery, rather than the fall-rise-fall pattern claimed for training time. Numerical values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Measures forgetting of HellaSwag accuracy when a pretrained model is continued-trained on duplicative data, which the authors call catastrophic forgetting. This is not test error on the training distribution over epochs near interpolation, so it cannot show or refute V2's fall-rise-fall shape. Values are figure only.
